C-LARGE-DOC-STAGE-0.Name: Large-document Stage 0: measurements and pre-refactor behavioral oracles
C-LARGE-DOC-STAGE-0.Summary: Mark has two independent O(document) cost trajectories — full-document mount on open (WebKit style/layout over ~30k DOM nodes on the accepted 1.7 MB / 9000-section shape) and full synchronous derived work plus history deep-copy on every edit — and today neither has a trustworthy Mark-specific baseline: the existing muya bench runs only initial render (PHASE_TYPING and PHASE_SCROLL are logged as SKIPPED stubs), and no characterization suite freezes save/close/move/metadata/external-change behavior before any refactor. Stage 0 closes exactly that gap and nothing else: it extends the existing bench with real-input-path typing and scroll measurement through the actual editable DOM pipeline, adds a deterministic generated fixture corpus (ordinary, size-scale, pathological-structure, expensive-leaf, semantic-edge and byte-policy shapes), measures component timings for both the opening and change hot paths across three evidence tiers (unit microbench, renderer CI in Chromium plus Playwright WebKit, real-app WKWebView acceptance), and commits characterization oracle suites that freeze current observable behavior — recording every known data-loss/false-clean defect family (dirty-tab liveReload silent overwrite, Move To/rename false-clean, line-ending/encoding/final-newline false-clean, overlapping-write reordering, close-by-tab-id races, in-place truncate/write saves, unregistered mt::save-tabs transport no-op Save All, string-only external equality, decode-to-String/UTF-8-writeback byte loss) as observedLegacyBehavior paired with a desiredInvariant, never as an accepted oracle. Stage 0 changes instrumentation and tests only; it ships no product behavior change, implements none of Waves A–D, and ends in an owner decision gate (target size, absolute and relative budgets, Wave A/B order, crash-durability contract, and later-wave experimental access model) recorded as machine-readable and human-readable evidence under the new routed performance module/verification pair M-060/V-M-060.

Problem.Description: Three blockers make any large-document optimization unsafe to start today. (1) No measured baseline: the only Mark-specific harness (src/renderer/bench) mounts the fixture and measures initial render, while its typing and scroll phases print SKIPPED stub markers (main.js, PHASE_TYPING/PHASE_SCROLL reason=stub-deferred-to-step-2.5b); the real costs of the change pipeline (Markdown serialization, the second cursor-marker serialization, word count, TOC, history deepCopy) are individually unmeasured, and source-mode behavior (CodeMirror viewportMargin: Infinity) is unverified as any kind of fallback. (2) No frozen behavioral oracle: the 2026-10-24 research packet identified multiple silent data-loss and false-clean paths in current save/close/move/metadata/external-write flows that no suite pins down, so a future optimization could regress them invisibly — and worse, a naive characterization could bless them as expected behavior. (3) Blocked product decisions: which cost trajectory to fix first (opening vs typing), the supported comfortable document size, the crash-durability contract, final absolute/relative budgets, and the later-wave experimental access model are owner decisions that must be forced by evidence, not guessed. The full pre-spec research packet (implementation plan, safety/verification matrix, two independent clean reviews) is preserved as design context for this change.

Goals.R-1: Fixture corpus: deterministic generated/sanitized fixtures committed with their generators and shape metadata — the existing ~4 KB bench fixture; ~100 KB mixed Markdown; ~1 MB and the accepted 1.7 MB/9000-section shape; one giant list; a 1000-row table; one giant paragraph/code block and a deeply nested list/blockquote; a math/image/diagram-heavy fixture with network disabled and assets local; a semantic edge corpus (link references, footnotes, setext headings, fences, task lists, tables, RU/EN); and a byte-policy corpus across supported UTF-8, UTF-16 LE/BE, Shift-JIS, GB2312, Latin-1, KOI8-R and CP-1251 with BOM, CRLF/mixed endings and final-newline variants. The non-UTF-8 byte-policy fixtures are byte-pinned in shape-metadata.json and materialized on demand by generators/ensure.mjs (the repository commit gate rejects non-UTF-8 blobs); the UTF-8 variants are committed. A 10 MB fixture is an optional local diagnostic, never a required CI fixture, unless the owner selects that target size.
Goals.R-2: Real-input typing measurement: the injector mutates the document through the actual user input pipeline (composition/input or beforeinput → Muya handler → contentState mutation → render → change/derived pipeline → next paint), asserting per measured edit that the expected Markdown changed and that undo restores the pre-edit value. Direct contentState mutation is permitted only as a separately labelled microbenchmark, never reported as the end-to-end typing number.
Goals.R-3: Scroll and responsiveness measurement: scroll frame-time distribution (jank, not average FPS only); input-to-next-paint p50/p95/max; longest main-thread task and count of tasks >50 ms where the Long Tasks API is available, otherwise a separately named event-loop-lag proxy — the two are never merged into one cross-engine series.
Goals.R-4: Component timings for both hot paths: file arrival → tab state, parse, vnode generation/patch/layout proxy, first visible content, time-to-input; Markdown serialization, cursor serialization, word count, TOC and history deep-copy durations; heap/retained-memory observations after open, edit pauses and tab close where the environment supports them, including C-68 opened-baseline retention and C-DOC-CHANGE-JOURNAL retention if that active change has landed (otherwise an explicit not-applicable state tied to its re-checked lifecycle); source-mode numbers recorded as explicitly not applicable in Stage 0 (the bench harness mounts Muya without the app shell and has no CodeMirror surface; the characterization suites own source-mode behavior); tab-close retained-memory and file-arrival-to-tab-state are likewise explicitly not applicable in the tab-less bench with that reason recorded; tail-mount completion recorded as explicitly not applicable in Stage 0 baselines (it exists only after Wave A).
Goals.R-5: Three required evidence tiers, extending the existing bench rather than replacing it: (1) pure/unit microbenchmarks isolating serializers, word count, TOC and history copy; (2) renderer CI on Chromium plus Playwright WebKit with deterministic fixtures and loose non-flaky ceilings; (3) real-app acceptance on system WKWebView + the Tauri/Rust artifact using BLOCK_* markers and exact fixture identity. Playwright WebKit evidence is labelled renderer/browser evidence, never native WKWebView. The stale bench README and the stale webkit-perf opt-in comment are corrected. Required Chromium and Playwright WebKit Stage 0 runs emit numeric PHASE_TYPING and PHASE_SCROLL results; an explicit not-run/unsupported label may describe only an optional diagnostic environment or unavailable optional metric and cannot satisfy either required phase or replace the real-app tier. Instrumentation/observer overhead is measured against an uninstrumented same-run control and reported separately.
Goals.R-6: Characterization oracle suites freezing current observable behavior at defined consistency boundaries: canonical Markdown and exact on-disk bytes; dirty/saved state and revision ownership; undo/redo grouping and clean/dirty transitions; word count/TOC/cursor/scroll at a forced boundary; typing, paste, cut, formatting, table/image/link operations, search/replace; deterministic mixed seeded edit/undo/redo/save/tab-switch/source/external-event sessions with the failing seed and minimized trace retained; styled HTML/PDF/print/DOCX and whole-document copy readers; save, Save As, save-and-close, Save All across named, untitled, successful and failing tabs (including the currently unregistered mt::save-tabs transport no-op) and quit payloads; workspace-replacement Save & Close; active- and background-tab-context Copy as Markdown, extension context and diff-mode entry; tab switch, split-view ownership and stale-owner isolation; Source Code mode round-trip; CJK/Pinyin/Hangul/dead-key IME composition, including older-timer and forced-reader interleavings across save, Save As, save-all, autosave, external-change, tab-switch, source, diff, export, copy, workspace-replace, rename, move, close and quit boundaries, and representative model mutations (format, replace, extension rewrite, history/reparse) fired while composition remains active; external-change comparison and diff baseline; text-equal but encoding/BOM/EOL/final-newline-different external rewrites; dirty named-document inline rename and Move To including cancel/failure/race cases; dirty-document line-ending/encoding/final-newline metadata changes followed by save/close/quit; navigation-only cursor/selection changes in WYSIWYG and Source Code that must not be misclassified as semantic edits; stale save acknowledgement followed by undo to the written revision; deliberately reordered overlapping save/autosave/save-all/close/workspace-replace backend completions asserting final disk bytes; edit-after-payload-before-close races for named close, Close All/window close, Quit and workspace replacement; Save As to a destination owned by a saved or dirty active/background tab, including case/symlink equivalence and an in-flight write; live-reference alias characterization for cursor/TOC/source maps plus a reusable future DTO contract scaffold; atomic-save watcher self-echo interleaved with a newer live edit; external modify/delete/replace after temp completion before destination commit including Save As expected-absent collision; crash/failure-point identification for a future displaced-version recovery state machine (marker reservation, exchange, preservation, restart reconciliation, resolution) or an explicitly recorded fail-closed non-CAS default until that fallback is separately approved; failure-point observation around the current in-place backend save path; and reusable fault-injection seams for future freshness failures. Current cross-window cases are recorded as not applicable because --new-window is a no-op; F-MULTI-WINDOW is the trigger for adding cross-window save/quit/session/recovery ownership coverage. Stage 0 does not implement ensureFreshDocument; suites establish the current oracle and reusable session drivers for future old/new differential execution. Random block keys, timestamps, DOM shape, internal history object shape and implementation-specific ordering are not frozen.
Goals.R-7: Known-defect dual recording: every characterization artifact for a known defect family carries two fields — observedLegacyBehavior (what current Mark does, asserted as today's fact) and desiredInvariant (the future acceptance gate). Only desiredInvariant may become a later acceptance criterion; in particular, the dirty-tab + liveReload=true silent overwrite, Move To/rename false-clean, metadata false-clean, overlapping-write reordering, close-by-tab-id, in-place save truncation, Save All transport no-op (mt::save-tabs), string-only external equality and UTF-8-writeback byte loss are recorded as failing scenarios, never as behavior to preserve.
Goals.R-8: Baseline evidence artifacts: machine-readable baseline JSON (commit, fixture hash, engine/runtime, run conditions) and a human-readable baseline table per fixture and engine, plus a cost breakdown for opening and typing, observer-overhead results, and supported retained-memory lifecycle observations.
Goals.R-9: Owner decision gate: Stage 0 delivers a short decision document forcing the owner's calls — confirmed target document size; approved absolute numeric budgets (first visible content, time-to-input, p95 input-to-next-paint, longest task, scroll) plus the same-run relative regression tolerance for ordinary documents and explicit platform/runtime labels; Wave A/B execution order; the crash-durability contract (no unsaved recovery + atomic old-or-new save, vs a separately approved durable-before-ack WAL — without an approved WAL there is no unsaved-recovery guarantee and none may be claimed); the later-wave experimental access model (visible Experimental setting, support-only preference, or private test artifact, always local/default-off/session-latched until a separately approved default flip); and the proposed next C-* boundary with observed write scope. The approved normative contract (target size, absolute/relative budgets, wave order, crash-durability contract, experimental access model) is recorded in the owning routed .grace/context document — either within Stage 0's approved scope or via a separately approved governance bundle that must land before any Wave A/B spec. No Wave A/B implementation starts before these outputs exist.
Goals.R-10: New governed performance harness module M-060 owns the Stage 0 benchmark drivers, deterministic fixture tooling and characterization-session harness, depends on the M-011 renderer ownership boundary and M-012 Muya engine without absorbing their product responsibilities, is owned by GD-PERFORMANCE in .grace/graph/performance.xml and routed through .grace/graph/index.xml, and has matching verification anchor V-M-060 owned by VD-PERFORMANCE in .grace/verification/performance.xml and routed through .grace/verification/index.xml. Existing M-011/M-012 narratives in .grace/graph/runtime.xml are updated for this explicit harness dependency/ownership handoff, and file-local LINKS are updated only in files inside Stage 0's own write scope (the bench harness and its new tooling); LINKS inside src/muya and other production files stay untouched — that side of the handoff is recorded in the graph narrative only. V-M-013-A is not repurposed and no anchor is duplicated.

Constraints.Item: Instrumentation and tests only: no production behavior change. editor.vue and store/editor.js production behavior is untouched; if timing markers in production files prove unavoidable, they are content-free, their overhead is measured, and active write scopes are reconciled first. Muya production code is not modified.

Known defects are characterized, not repaired, not blessed: Stage 0 neither fixes the defect families listed in R-7 nor turns any of them into an approval oracle. Each repair is a separate prerequisite change that must land or be declared an explicit dependency before the corresponding later-wave rollout.

Truthfulness of evidence: Playwright WebKit results are labelled browser evidence; real WKWebView runs record artifact/commit and generated-fixture hashes; the typing injector provably drives the real input path; skipped optional diagnostics are reported as skipped, while a skipped PHASE_TYPING/PHASE_SCROLL in a required Chromium or Playwright WebKit run fails the Stage 0 gate.

Privacy: no private document text, selected text, private paths or secrets enter the repository or retained artifacts. Private acceptance inputs use opaque local IDs and rounded shape metadata or a non-committed salted/HMAC mapping — never committed unsalted hashes, traces, screenshots or logs. New Stage 0 markers use opaque fixture/tab IDs; artifact collection allowlists or sanitizes retained lines (current legacy logs are not assumed path-free); private acceptance captures stay uncommitted. Global legacy log cleanup is separate scope.

Pre-existing GRACE baseline is recorded, not silently inherited: in the pre-spec capture immediately before this bundle was created, at commit ea4ddcd7540b2fa0968cad1c55cadd5685b7d5f9 (branch train/2.8.1-seal-squash, 2026-10-24), the working tree carried 81 uncommitted entries from parallel sessions; grace status reported 10 active changes, 7 integrity errors, 19 warnings; grace lint --assertions current = 7 errors / 19 warnings (all pre-existing MODULE_MAP drift); grace lint --parallel-preflight = 24 errors / 19 warnings (observed-write and durable-scope overlaps among active changes, including this change's future .grace/graph/*.xml and .grace/verification/*.xml writes against the broad scopes of C-50, C-FILE-POSITION-MEMORY, C-NOTIFICATION-SYSTEM and others). Adding this draft bundle itself makes the live counts 82 entries and 11 active changes without changing those lint totals. The plan must distinguish pre-existing findings from change-introduced ones and must not be approved or executed until every actual overlap is sequenced, narrowed or completed; the snapshot in this constraint is re-verified, not trusted, at plan time.

Existing CI gates stay green and are not weakened: V-M-025 open-file timing, the webkit-perf project inside mandatory renderer-e2e, and webkit-session. New CI ceilings (if any) are loose, non-flaky and separately justified; hard numeric budgets are owner-approved only after Stage 0, never guessed in it.

Execution safety (binding on the later plan even though this pass does not execute): dedicated isolated worktree; no destructive reset/checkout in the shared dirty tree; full docs/commit-push-safety.md before any commit/push; hooks intact; required protected checks status check, release/governance and release/readiness. Green checks and a merged change never imply release authorization; this work is backlogged product improvement, not a reopened FIX-002 defect and not automatically queued for any release train.
m048 is a compile-time capability map, not a runtime feature flag; no feature flag is introduced by Stage 0. A public -beta tag is never used as a private cohort because it advances /releases/latest.

English repo artifacts throughout; governed files keep MODULE_CONTRACT/MODULE_MAP/CHANGE_SUMMARY accurate; fixture generators and committed suites carry appropriate contracts (TEST/SCRIPT role with LOCALS map proposed; final decision at plan time); graph and verification deltas land in the same bundle as the tests.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Wave A progressive mount; Wave B1 change-source contract; Wave B2 lazy derived-state pipeline (including ensureFreshDocument); Wave B3 history materialization redesign — all remain design context until separately speced after the Stage 0 decision gate.
Wave C large-file warnings, thresholds, guards or graceful degradation, and Wave D virtualization/engine migration.
content-visibility rollout (stays default-off on macOS until a disproving experiment of its own).

Any repair of the recorded defect families (liveReload overwrite, Move To/rename, metadata false-clean, write ordering, save-and-close identity, atomic save, Save All transport, external equality, encoding preservation F-ENCODING-WRITE-PRESERVE): Stage 0 observes and records; each fix is its own prerequisite change.

Any durable crash-recovery/WAL work or any claim of hard-crash recovery: without a separately approved WAL, a hard crash may lose all edits since the last committed save (an untitled buffer in full), and the current in-place save can damage even the previous file; Stage 0 tests state this honestly.
Production default changes, feature flags, release actions, or train admission of any kind.

Global cleanup of path-bearing legacy logs; a required 10 MB CI fixture (stays optional diagnostic unless the owner selects that target); cherry-picking upstream marktext PR #4946 or ColaMD code (they are design references only).
Creating plan.xml in this pass; the plan is a separate grace-plan pass with its own explicit owner approval.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Fixture corpus committed and deterministic: generators plus generated/sanitized fixtures for every R-1 shape including the byte-policy matrix; the non-UTF-8 byte-policy fixtures are byte-pinned by sha256 and materialized on demand by generators/ensure.mjs because the repository commit gate rejects non-UTF-8 blobs, while every UTF-8 variant is committed; regenerating yields identical bytes for committed fixtures and the same sha256 for every materialized one; no private content or unsalted private-input fingerprints are committed.

Typing truthfulness: the end-to-end typing suite proves the injector drives the real input pipeline — expected Markdown changes after each measured edit and undo restores the pre-edit value — in both the Chromium and Playwright WebKit renderer tiers; their required PHASE_TYPING and PHASE_SCROLL runs produce numeric results. Explicit not-run/unsupported labels are allowed only for optional diagnostic environments or metrics, do not satisfy either required phase and cannot replace the real-app tier.

Metrics coverage: per fixture and engine, the harness emits first visible content, time-to-input, input-to-next-paint p50/p95/max, longest task + >50 ms count (or the separately named event-loop-lag proxy), scroll frame-time distribution, parse/vnode/patch/layout proxies, serialization/cursor/word-count/TOC/history-copy timings, heap/retained-memory lifecycle observations where supported, observer overhead against an uninstrumented same-run control, and source-mode numbers separately labelled where the harness has a source surface (otherwise explicitly not applicable with the reason recorded), with tab-close memory, file-arrival-to-tab-state and tail-mount completion explicitly recorded as not applicable until their harness exists.

Characterization suites committed covering the R-6 scenario list, including CJK/Pinyin/Hangul/dead-key composition, mixed seeded sessions with retained failing seed/minimized trace, editing operations and controlled readers, deliberately reordered backend completions asserting final disk bytes, IME interleavings across the full boundary set (save, Save As, save-all, autosave, external change, tab switch, source, diff, export, copy, workspace replace, rename, move, close, quit), displaced-version/fail-closed failure-point identification, and byte-policy round-trips where the renderer harness owns the decode path (non-UTF decode is backend-owned and recorded as not applicable in the renderer harness, with the lossy-decode cases labelled observedLegacyBehavior); every known-defect artifact carries observedLegacyBehavior and desiredInvariant fields.

Baseline artifacts produced: machine-readable JSON with commit, fixture hash, engine/runtime and run conditions, plus the human-readable baseline table and opening/typing cost breakdown, sufficient to found the R-9 owner decisions.

Graph and verification routing: M-060 owns the Stage 0 harness/tooling boundary, declares its M-011/M-012 dependencies in .grace/graph/performance.xml and is routed through .grace/graph/index.xml; matching V-M-060 exists in .grace/verification/performance.xml and is routed through .grace/verification/index.xml with the Stage 0 commands, scenarios and content-free markers; M-011/M-012 narratives and file-local LINKS reflect the dependency handoff, with LINKS edits confined to Stage 0-owned files and no src/muya file touched; no existing anchor is repurposed or duplicated; existing V-M-025/webkit-perf/webkit-session gates remain green.

No production behavior change: outside allowlisted content-free timing markers in editor.vue/store/editor.js (if any), no diffs in editor.vue, store/editor.js or src/muya production files — src/muya admits no markers and no diffs at all; npm test green; grace lint --assertions current reports no new errors beyond the recorded pre-existing baseline.

Owner decision document delivered with baseline tables, cost breakdowns, the five decision questions (target size, absolute/relative budgets, Wave A/B order, crash contract, experimental access model) and the proposed next C-* boundary; it names where the approved contract durably lands (.grace/context/ux-guidelines.xml after the owner decides — a follow-up governed step here or a separate governance bundle that must land before any Wave A/B spec) and explicitly states that no release or train admission follows automatically.

Documentation truthfulness: the stale bench README and the stale webkit-perf opt-in comment in playwright.config.ts are corrected to describe actual behavior (typing/scroll phases as implemented by this change) and the mandatory CI status of webkit-perf in renderer-e2e.

AffectedAreas.Item: src/renderer/bench/ — main.js (typing/scroll phases become real), README.md (corrected contracts), run-bench.mjs and/or a new focused driver; MODULE_CONTRACT/MAP updates in the same bundle.
Deterministic fixture generators and generated fixtures under the existing test fixture area (exact location at plan time).

Focused new suites under tests/renderer/ and tests/e2e/perf/; playwright.config.ts — the one-line stale webkit-perf opt-in comment correction (near line 49) plus project routing changes if any; .github/workflows/test.yml only if a stable new CI gate is intentionally admitted.

.grace/context/ux-guidelines.xml — the recorded performance principle gains the approved Stage 0 contract (target size, budgets, wave order, crash contract, experimental access model) once the owner decides it; the write happens in the follow-up governed step or a separate bundle, not in this change's execution.

.grace/graph/performance.xml + .grace/graph/index.xml — new governed harness module M-060 owns Stage 0 benchmark drivers, deterministic fixture tooling and characterization-session harness; M-011/M-012 narratives and LINKS record its renderer/Muya dependencies.
.grace/graph/runtime.xml — narrow narrative edit limited to the M-011/M-012 dependency/ownership handoff statements (GD-RUNTIME-owned document; no other anchors touched).
Explicitly out of write scope: editor.vue and store/editor.js production behavior, src/muya production code, any Rust backend behavior.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedCommand: npx vitest run <new focused suites> && npx playwright test <new behavioral suites> --project=chromium && npx playwright test <WebKit suites> --project=webkit-perf --project=webkit-session && node src/renderer/bench/run-bench-preview.mjs (or the plan-approved focused driver) emitting numeric PHASE_TYPING/PHASE_SCROLL for the Chromium tier — the Playwright chromium project ignores **/perf/**, so the Chromium bench tier runs through the bench driver, never a Playwright project — && npm test (exact file lists, driver invocation and ordering are fixed by the approved plan)
VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Required Chromium and Playwright WebKit real-input typing/scroll numbers with truthfulness assertions; the R-6 characterization matrix green with known defects dual-recorded; baseline JSON + human table with commit and fixture hashes, observer overhead and supported retained-memory lifecycle observations; M-060/V-M-060 routed with content-free markers; existing V-M-025/webkit-perf/webkit-session gates green; npm test green; grace lint delta clean against the recorded pre-existing baseline. Pre-implementation active-baseline check: grace lint --path . --assertions current and --parallel-preflight re-run before any write; this evidence is the change's own gate, not a final-state claim. Real-app WKWebView acceptance runs the plan-built Mark.app, is recorded with the exact artifact commit and generated-fixture hashes, and passes when the driver emits numeric PHASE_TYPING and PHASE_SCROLL results and the typed character lands in the measured block; it stays outside CI as owner-reviewed evidence; because that run happens on the owner side, an absent capture is recorded as pending and is never replaced by a not-run label.

Assumptions.Assumption: The 2026-10-24 implementation packet is the canonical design context: its five normative-input files (00-README, 05-implementation-plan, 06-safety-verification-matrix, 07-spec-author-handoff, 10-source-and-evidence-index) hash exactly to the SHA-256 values pinned by both independent clean reviews (verified 2026-10-24 before drafting); the preserved 04-safety-review debounce-bounded crash claim is rejected per the packet's explicit errata — without a WAL, all unsaved edits can be lost.

Active-change states as re-checked 2026-10-24: C-FILE-POSITION-MEMORY is implemented in the working tree but uncommitted; C-DOC-CHANGE-JOURNAL has an approved spec and no plan; C-50, C-GITHUB-THEME, C-NOTIFICATION-SYSTEM, C-NATIVE-DOCX-RTF-EXPORT, C-RELEASE-TIMING, C-36, C-37, C-47 remain active with broad observed scopes. All states are re-verified at plan time; the packet snapshot is not authority.
M-060 and V-M-060 are unused across .grace graph and verification indexes as of 2026-10-24; the plan confirms both ids remain available before claiming the required pair.

The 1.7 MB/9000-section shape remains the accepted backlog reference target ("first paint in a few hundred milliseconds"); Stage 0 measures it but does not presuppose the owner's final size answer, and ordinary-document budgets stay unchanged.

Renderer CI can run Chromium and Playwright WebKit deterministically enough for loose non-flaky ceilings (it already runs webkit-perf mandatorily); real WKWebView acceptance runs are local/owner-reviewed, not CI gates.
